confidence_notes: I used four of the six allowed searches: one for the exchange rate and three for food and drink prices. Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are based on Numbeo's Tulum page labelled Nov 2026, as summarised in search results: inexpensive meal about MXN 150, cappuccino about MXN 71, domestic draft pint about MXN 55, mid-range meal for two about MXN 1,000. Older aggregators such as Traveltables and Expat Exchange show lower figures. Numbeo has few contributors for Tulum and its ranges are wide. I converted pesos at about 17.5 MXN per USD, an assumed rate for July 2026 that I did not search for. I raised beer slightly above the Numbeo median because tourist-area restaurant prices are usually higher. Cocktail and wine are less certain. They come from a few restaurant menus seen in search results: cocktails about MXN 134 to 285 and wine glasses about MXN 173 to 360. They are also cross-checked against their usual price relationship to beer. Beach-zone and beach-club venues can charge two or more times these amounts. The accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge and were not checked against any listings. Tulum's room prices are high for Mexico and change a lot with season and location (town versus beach zone). July is usually mid or shoulder season. FX caveat: the search results gave the RBA 4.00 pm reference rate for 18 November 2026 as 0.6720 USD per AUD. That value came from a site that republishes RBA data. The rba.gov.au page below appeared in the results, but I did not open it to confirm the figure.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based mainly on aggregated Tulum prices, which are above Mexican averages. For accommodation, I benchmarked against other Riviera Maya tourist towns such as Playa del Carmen and Cancun's hotel zone, adjusted upward for Tulum's boutique, upscale market.
